finding: DSPy represents language-model calls through signatures and composable modules/programs, allowing a system to be described structurally instead of as a single prompt string.
locator: Paper §2 and §3; pinned README and module API
scope_limit: Program abstraction does not itself specify a protected improvement/evaluation authority boundary.

finding: Teleprompter/optimizer compiles a declared student program by selecting demonstrations/instructions and may include fine-tuning routes; it changes the candidate program artifact, not its own optimizer algorithm or evaluation definition.
locator: Paper optimization discussion; dspy/teleprompt/bootstrap.py: BootstrapFewShot; dspy/teleprompt/mipro_optimizer_v2.py: compile
scope_limit: Different DSPy optimizers expose different candidate spaces; this crosswalk focuses on the pinned BootstrapFewShot/MIPROv2 path.

finding: The caller supplies the metric. BootstrapFewShot uses it to accept/reject traces; MIPROv2 passes it to its Evaluate instance for scoring candidates on valset.
locator: dspy/teleprompt/bootstrap.py: constructor and _bootstrap_one_example; dspy/teleprompt/mipro_optimizer_v2.py: constructor and compile
scope_limit: The framework does not make the metric independent by construction; metric may be a deterministic function or model-based judge selected by the application.

finding: MIPROv2 requires trainset and accepts optional valset. At the pinned commit, if valset is omitted it splits a subset of the supplied trainset to form a validation set; this is a local split, not a separately protected holdout.
scope_limit: The split behavior is version-specific and should not be generalized to every DSPy optimizer or release.

finding: BootstrapFewShot runs a teacher program over training examples, optionally at varied rollouts, captures traces, and accepts traces according to the caller metric/threshold before compiling demonstrations.
scope_limit: Bootstrapped traces are derived from the supplied training examples and model; they are not independently adjudicated data by default.

finding: Candidate scoring uses the supplied metric and validation subset. The optimizer can consume task/program/data-aware proposals; no intrinsic non-writable external evaluator or sealed release gate is established by the inspected API.
locator: Paper metric-driven compilation; MIPROv2 compile and Evaluate call
scope_limit: Application designers can add external controls; the claim is that this mechanism alone does not supply them.

finding: Compiled program artifacts can be saved/used as a program configuration; successful demos and optimized instructions can be reused with the same declared program structure.
locator: README; dspy/teleprompt/bootstrap.py: compile and _train; optimizer serialization utilities
scope_limit: Artifact reuse does not guarantee equivalent behavior across models/providers or new task distributions.

finding: DSPy exposes LM abstractions and optional integrations while supporting configurable task and prompt models. Pinned package dependencies include LiteLLM and optional provider adapters.
scope_limit: API/provider configurability is not evidence of cross-provider method transfer or equivalent outputs.

finding: A held-out validation subset can be formed from trainset when omitted in the pinned MIPROv2 path, but it remains drawn from the same user-supplied corpus; a protected test set, contamination protocol, immutable metric, and release authority remain application responsibilities.
locator: Pinned MIPROv2 dataset split and paper metric-driven optimizer
scope_limit: No leakage or benchmark contamination is asserted for any particular DSPy run.

finding: A local DSPy optimizer can optimize prompts/demos/modules that are part of an application's harness/program, but the comparison to Harness-RSI is an analogy; DSPy does not by itself implement MetaRSI's three-surface scheduler or recursive method-policy update.
locator: Crosswalk of DSPy v1 framing/code and MetaRSI v2 surface taxonomy
scope_limit: This comparison is research-only and does not recommend adding DSPy to Pointfire.
